newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares bounce to close up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares bounce to close up in thin trade.

text.p: Brazilian stocks regained ground lost in recent sessions, closing up on rising volume due to bargain buying and mirroring hikes in the Dow and regional markets, brokers said.
"Markets all over the region were up today," one dealer said, adding investors returned to Brazil's bolsas after depressed trade on Monday and Friday attracted by cheap blue-chip prices.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of .BVSP of 52 most traded shares rose 980 points to end at 61,261 points, up 1.63 percent from Monday, on volume totalling 323 million reais.
While volume was thin, it was up from anemic levels in recent sessions as large local investors took advantage of cheap prices to nap up benchmark Telebras and other blue chips, brokers said.
The rise in Sao Paulo was aided by a 3.4 percent surge in Argentina's MerVal index and the Mexican bolsa's new record- high close, as well as a hike in the Dow Jones, they said.
"The internal market was calm, but it was pushed upwards by overseas," one broker said. "Large local players were all active after yesterday's speculative selling."
